author: LegalEagle
description:
A man tried to argue his appeal through an AI-generated lawyer, and the judge caught it within seconds 🎭

Jerome Dewald, who isn't a lawyer, was representing himself in his case against MassMutual at a March 26, 2025 hearing in a New York appeals court. The court allowed him to accompany his oral argument with a pre-recorded video presentation. What he didn't disclose was that the speaker in the video was a digital avatar he had created with AI software.

The avatar opened with "May it please the court." Within seconds, a justice stopped the video and asked whether the speaker was counsel for the case. Dewald admitted he had generated it and that it wasn't a real person.

He later apologized to the court, explaining that he thought the avatar could deliver his argument without his usual mumbling, stumbling, and tripping over words. Still, the AI avatar wasn't a real lawyer, and it definitely didn't please the court.

Follow us for more on AI's messy arrival in the courtroom!

#Law #La
title: It Took a Judge Seconds to Catch This Man's AI Lawyer
